extracted.intended_audience: motor vehicle manufacturers, suppliers, test laboratories, and regulatory compliance/legal staff
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and test procedures for seat belt assembly anchorages under the amended Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS No. 210), including optional use of Force Application Devices (FADs), body block placement zones, strength criteria, timelines, and related regulatory analyses and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead time for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency provides a two-year lead time for both continued use of the current body blocks and optional use of the Force Application Device (FAD). Consistent with 49 CFR 571.8(b), multi-stage manufacturers and alterers have an additional year (total of three years) to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers may continue to certify using body blocks if they prefer or need additional time to certify using the FAD; the two-year lead time is intended to allow manufacturers to become familiar with the new zones and test device. The rule notes historical use of body blocks since 1970 and expects limited redesign need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturer's choice of compliance option (S4.2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The manufacturer shall select the compliance option (body block procedure or FAD procedure) by the time it certifies the vehicle and may not thereafter select a different option for that vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon request by NHTSA, manufacturers must provide which compliance option was selected for a particular vehicle or make/model. Manufacturers that cannot or will not use FADs may continue to certify to the body block procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength requirement for Type 1 and certain Type 2 seat belt assemblies (S4.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchorages, attachment hardware, and attachment bolts for Type 1 seat belt assemblies and the lap belt portion of certain Type 2/automatic seat belt assemblies must withstand 22,241 N (5,000 pounds) when tested per the specified procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability dates: vehicles manufactured on or after September 17, 2024 and before September 1, 2027 may use S5.1(a), (b), or (c); vehicles manufactured on or after September 1, 2027 must use S5.1(b) or (c). Manufacturer chooses test procedure option at certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength requirement for certain Type 2 and automatic seat belt assemblies (S4.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchorages, attachment hardware, and bolts for certain Type 2 and automatic seat belt assemblies must withstand simultaneous application of 13,345 N (3,000 pounds) to the lap belt and 13,345 N (3,000 pounds) to the shoulder belt when tested per the specified procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability dates: vehicles manufactured on or after September 17, 2024 and before September 1, 2027 may use S5.2(a), (b), or (c); vehicles manufactured on or after September 1, 2027 must use S5.2(b) or (c). Manufacturer chooses test procedure option at certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: General test provisions (S5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a range of values is specified, the vehicle must meet the requirements at all points within the range; anchorage shall be connected to material whose breaking strength is equal to or greater than the breaking strength of the installed seat belt webbing; the geometry of the attachment must duplicate the geometry of the originally installed seat belt at initiation of the test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures tests reflect actual installation strength and geometry; applies regardless of whether body blocks or FADs are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat adjustment for testing (S5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If adjustable, the seat must be placed using any seat adjustment controls into the configurations and positions of the rearmost normal design driving or riding position consistent with the seating reference point (SgRP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Rearmost’ is relative to the direction the seat faces. The seat may face any direction in which it can be occupied while the vehicle is in motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shoulder belt anchorage height adjustment (S5(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The shoulder belt anchorage height adjustment (D-ring) may be set to any height for the test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flexibility to set D-ring height; manufacturers should record settings used in tests to support certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body block test procedure for 5,000 lb (S5.1(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a 22,241 N (5,000 lb) force in the direction the seat faces to a pelvic body block (figure 2A), in a plane parallel to the seat reference plane with an initial force application angle of 5–15 degrees above horizontal; apply at an onset rate of not more than 222,411 N/s, attain the force in not more than 30 seconds, and maintain for 10 seconds. Optionally, pelvic body block of figure 2B may be substituted for groups of three or more anchorages per S4.2.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exact force, angle, onset rate, attainment time, and duration. Use of figure 2B pelvic block permitted for center sets of multiple anchorages.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAD test procedure for 5,000 lb (S5.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose FAD(s) per S5.4 and position per S5.5. Apply a 22,241 N (5,000 lb) force to the actuator attachment point of the bridged pull yoke attached to the FAD1 or FAD2, in the direction the seat faces, plane parallel to seat reference plane, initial force angle 5–15 degrees above horizontal; onset rate ≤ 222,411 N/s, attain in ≤ 30 seconds, maintain for 10 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAD(s) are an optional alternative to body blocks; manufacturer must follow S5.4 (choice) and S5.5 (positioning). Procedure mirrors body block force/time/angle requirements but applies force to FAD actuator/bridged pull yoke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body block positioning variation for 5,000 lb (S5.1(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the 22,241 N (5,000 lb) force to a pelvic body block as in S5.1(a) but with the pelvic body block positioned in accordance with S5.3.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S5.3.1 contains the specified placement procedure (zones/placements); manufacturer may use this placement approach as an alternative to the earlier-described position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body & upper-torso simultaneous test procedure for 3,000 lb (S5.2(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply simultaneous 13,345 N (3,000 lb) forces in the direction the seat faces to a pelvic body block (figure 2A) and an upper torso body block (figure 3), plane parallel to seat reference plane, initial force angle 5–15 degrees above horizontal; apply at onset rate ≤ 133,447 N/s, attain force in ≤ 30 seconds, and maintain for 10 seconds. Optionally, pelvic body block figure 2B may be substituted for multiple-anchorage groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies simultaneous lap and shoulder loading with exact force, angle, onset rate, attainment time, and duration. Use of figure 2B pelvic block permitted for groups of anchorages as in S5.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAD test procedure for simultaneous 3,000 lb (S5.2(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose FAD(s) per S5.4 and position per S5.5 to apply the simultaneous 13,345 N (3,000 lb) forces to the lap and shoulder attachment points as required for S4.2.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAD-based procedure mirrors the body/torso block simultaneous load requirements; manufacturer must follow S5.4/S5.5 for device selection/positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and incorporation by reference of FAD and components (S3 and §571.5 additions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines key terms used by the standard: Actuator; Bridged pull yoke; FAD (Force Application Device – FAD1 or FAD2); FAD1 (larger version; drawings NHTSA221-210-01); FAD2 (smaller version; drawings NHTSA221-210-01J); Midsagittal plane; Seat reference plane. Specifies incorporation by reference of drawing packages for FAD1 and FAD2 into §571.210.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers and test labs must use the incorporated drawings when selecting/constructing FADs. The definitions clarify how the devices are used in S5.1/S5.2 test procedures and how positioning relates to the seat reference plane/midsagittal plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body block placement zones (clarification of test procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule adds specified zones within which the agency will place body blocks during compliance testing, restricting agency discretion and making the test more objective and repeatable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zones are intended to reduce re-testing and increase repeatability. NHTSA states the zone specification is a clarification and does not change strength requirements; manufacturers are given two years to become familiar with zone placement. The preamble explains that SAE J384 does not specify zones and that this deviation is justified to ensure enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional use of FADs and economic/procurement considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The FADs (FAD1 and FAD2) are an optional alternative to body blocks. Estimated unit cost ≈ $8,000; illustrative set of two FAD1s and three FAD2s estimated at $40,000. FADs require less effort, time, and personnel to install; FAD2 is smaller to fit DSPs that cannot accommodate FAD1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because FADs are optional, manufacturers can avoid purchase cost by continuing to use body blocks. NHTSA notes potential time savings in setup that could offset purchase costs. Comments indicated lead time and marketplace availability concerns for FAD procurement; agency provided two-year optional lead time to address these concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 603(b) of the Regulatory Flexibility Act specifies that each RFA must contain: (1) reasons why agency action is being considered; (2) succinct statement of objectives and legal basis for the rule; (3) description and estimate of number of small entities to which final rule applies; (4) description of projected reporting/recordkeeping/compliance requirements including classes of small entities affected and professional skills necessary; (5) identification of relevant Federal rules which may duplicate/overlap/conflict; (6) description of significant alternatives that minimize economic impact on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA used certification (no significant impact on a substantial number of small entities) rather than a full initial RFA and explains factual basis in the preamble. Agencies must provide these elements when an RFA is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language considerations for rule drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Orders 12866 and 13563 require agencies to use plain language; consider: organization to suit public needs; clarity of requirements; avoidance of unclear technical jargon; use of different formatting (headings, paragraphing) to improve understandability; whether more but shorter sections would help; whether tables, lists, or diagrams would improve clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA states it considered these questions in drafting and invites public suggestions for improving plain language in the rule. Agencies should apply these checklist items when writing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of confidential business information (CBI) procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters submitting confidential information must provide: a redacted public version of the comment and a request for confidential treatment to the Office of Chief Counsel per 49 CFR part 512. One unredacted 'confidential version' must be submitted to the Office of Chief Counsel with required labeling; one redacted 'public version' must also be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per §512.6, pages with claimed confidentiality must include 'ENTIRE PAGE CONFIDENTIAL BUSINESS INFORMATION' or 'CONFIDENTIAL BUSINESS INFORMATION CONTAINED WITHIN BRACKETS'. When not all information on a page is confidential, identify each confidential item within brackets. Requests must set forth required supporting information per part 512; submit requests electronically to the Office of Chief Counsel (contact emails provided) or via secure file transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption and severability analyses and statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Executive Order 13132 and related statutes, NHTSA must examine whether a rule has federalism implications or preemptive effect. The standard notes: FMVSS are generally minimum standards under 49 U.S.C. 30103(b)(1); express preemption applies to non-identical State standards; a savings clause preserves State common law causes of action; NHTSA finds this rule does not intend to preempt State tort law because it prescribes a minimum standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should analyze whether the regulatory text and objectives indicate preemption of State law or tort causes of action. Severability is governed by 49 CFR 571.9: if any FMVSS or its application is held invalid, the remainder and other applications are unaffected.
